The event-implied move is 13.4%, from a 23-day straddle of 17.2% net of ordinary vol. The quote is indicative only: the ATM spread is 80% of mid, and the put/call OI ratio is 0.17. No dated FINV consensus was reachable. Aggregators show next-year revenue estimates cut about 11% over 3 months. At roughly 236m ADS (Q2 weighted basic) the market cap is about $560m, against about $946m of cash plus short-term investments at 2026-06-30. The scored exit is the opening print of Friday 2026-11-27, a half-day session after Thanksgiving.
view: This is a depressed China loan facilitator, reporting the morning after its largest peer showed the sector is still deteriorating. The direction of the news is bad, but the price has already moved a long way to meet it. Three things decide the open: whether the FY revenue guide survives at the RMB11.5bn low end, how far credit metrics and provisions have slipped (Qfin's 30-day collection fell to 86.0% and its day-1 delinquency rose to 5.8%), and whether capital return continues. My rough arithmetic says the revenue guide is not obviously broken. H1 was RMB6,613m, so the low end needs about RMB4.89bn in H2. Suppose overseas holds at about RMB0.95-1.0bn a quarter and China revenue falls 20-30% from Q2's RMB2,473m (revenue lags volume because guarantee and post-origination fees trail). Then Q3 lands around RMB2.7-3.0bn and Q4 needs only about RMB1.9-2.2bn. So a formal revenue cut is possible but not forced. The overseas leg, 27% of revenue and growing, is a cushion Qfin does not have. Profit and a Q4 tone like Qfin's 'extra cautious' stance are the downside risk. So is a softer buyback ('prioritize steady operations first'). Against that, the stock already sits at its 52-week low below its cash, and it took the Qfin read-through today. Historically the open has carried only part of the reaction, and a thin half-day Friday open adds noise. I cannot find a dated datapoint the price is missing in either direction. Slightly bearish, close to a coin flip.

recommendation.reason: The sector news since FINV last spoke is negative: Qfin's Q4 guide cut, its 'liquidity squeeze' and its credit erosion. But FINV fell 4.4% today in sympathy and 17.6% over 20 days, and it trades below its cash. Its revenue guide has an overseas cushion that makes a hold at the low end plausible. I cannot show a gap between what the price holds and what the release will reveal, so I make no call.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Either of two things would make this a clear short: a formal cut of the FY26 revenue guide below RMB11.5bn, or a Q4 profit outlook like Qfin's together with a paused buyback. Either of two would make it a long: a reaffirmed guide with the buyback continuing, or a new or enlarged buyback or special dividend.

self_critique: The bearish case is stronger than my 46 implies. Qfin cut its Q4 guide sharply and fell 9.5% even after a 46% slide, so a deeply de-rated stock is no floor. FINV management already said 'lower part unless the environment substantially changes', and Qfin's commentary says it did change. FINV's credit metrics were starting to worsen in August, with early risk indicators up 20%. And the Q2 open gap was small (-3.5%) before a -15% close, so the open may also understate a bad print. The bullish case is that FINV fell with Qfin today and the overseas leg protects revenue. Either way, I cannot settle the decisive line, whether the guide is cut, before the release.
